sentence: This project studies how people learn computer-aided design and which factors besides 3D thinking skills shape that learning.
This project studies the strong nuclear force by analyzing collisions of heavy nuclei and helping build a detector and an AI chatbot.
This project uses coral records to find out how Red Sea surface water temperature and salinity changed over time and how that affects deep ocean circulation.
This project builds a neural probe made of silicon carbide that records electrical activity and delivers light to stimulate neurons in the brain for a long time.
This project builds a robot inspired by mud-dwelling fishes that senses wet sandy and muddy ground and changes how it moves to cross it.
This project builds mathematical methods that handle problems where the number of possible configurations grows exponentially, such as in quantum materials and molecular systems.
This project studies human-AI interaction in Web and information systems, using datasets and machine learning models.
This project studies how silver nanoparticles disrupt proteins that control the shape and growth of brain cells, using cells in culture and a nematode worm.
This project turns a pilot data service into a national system that connects researchers to scientific data wherever it is stored.
This project builds control algorithms for autonomous vehicles and delivery drones that stay reliable even when the computation is stopped early.
This project uses computer simulations and deep learning to study how electrical, mechanical and fluid processes in the heart lead to cardiac arrhythmias.
This project uses simulations and deep learning to study how peptides on surfaces form nanoscale patterns that change how the surface interacts with water.
This project studies cybersecurity and artificial intelligence in areas such as smart homes, transportation and healthcare.
This project uses geochemical data in ancient soils to find out whether heat and dryness caused grasslands to become shrublands over the past 30,000 years.
This project uses algebra and geometry to find keystone species in microbial communities and tests them with laboratory experiments.
This project studies what genomic sequencing data can and cannot reveal and builds efficient algorithms to align, reconstruct and cluster DNA sequences.
This project builds mass spectrometry methods that use laser light and ion separation to work out the structures of nucleic acids.
